sam_sullivan (sales): Heads-up — AtlasHealth (dedicated customer) reported a sharp throughput drop and p95 jump since ~2026-03-18 22:00 UTC. They say requests/sec fell ~3x and p95 went from ~120ms to ~980ms. They have an SLA and are asking for a timeline. Link to customer dashboard: https://redwood.internal/atlashealth/dashboards/throughput

anika_patel (support): Attached metrics snapshot and a short excerpt of their logs. No config changes on their end. They did note increased batch wait times in client logs.

jia_wu (eng-oncall): Thanks. Can we get the dedicated instance id and recent deploy history? Any runtime/runtime-kernel changes rolled to dedicated yesterday? Also pinging ops-bot for recent infra events.

ops-bot: Incident monitor: no cluster-wide infra events between 2026-03-18T20:00Z and 2026-03-19T02:00Z. New runtime release tag: rtx-3.14.1 rolled to staged on 2026-03-18T21:30Z, rolled to dedicated pools for some customers at 2026-03-18T22:05Z.

marco_garcia (eng-runtime): Noted. rtx-3.14.1 included a kernel-selection heuristic change and more aggressive KV-cache eviction to reduce memory pressure. That could blow up tail latency if eviction interacts with long-lived sessions. Quick check: can you provide instance id + trace id for slow request? Also send gpu_util and nvlink error counts.

anika_patel (support): Instance: ded-az2-78. Example trace id: atlh-20260318-5567. Attaching client slow-request snippet: ``REQUEST TRACE atlh-20260318-5567: wait_for_batch 420ms, compute_start 390ms, compute_end 920ms, total 1310ms``

jia_wu (eng-oncall): That pattern (long wait_for_batch + compute spike) smells like batching/queueing + compute kernel slowdown. First action: flip on fallback to previous runtime for AtlasHealth only. Leah, do we have permission to patch their pool?

leah_ng (product): Atlas is enterprise contracted, SLA priority is high. We should aim for a config-only mitigation immediately and a code rollback as a follow-up if needed. Please keep support and sales updated with ETA.

marco_garcia (eng-runtime): I'll open an emergency rollback for that customer to rtx-3.13.8 and disable aggressive eviction for their pool. Quick commands (eng-only): ``curl -X POST https://controlplane.internal/pools/ded-az2-78/override -d '{"runtime":"rtx-3.13.8","kv_eviction":"off"}'``

jia_wu (eng-oncall): I'll run quick checks to confirm. Can someone grab GPU metrics around the spike window? Command: ``kubectl --context=ded-az2-78 logs -l app=inference -c metrics --since=4h | jq .gpu_util``

marco_garcia (eng-runtime): Also check host swap/oom events and any NVML errors: ``/usr/local/bin/nvmlmon --since 4h``. If we see NVML errors, that points at driver/TLS issues rather than runtime heuristics.

anika_patel (support): Noted. I've told AtlasHealth we're investigating and will provide a mitigation within 2 hours. They reported customer impact on 2 of 4 endpoints: chat and embeddings.

leah_ng (product): Prioritization: this is customer-impacting P1 for a contracted Dedicated customer. Create backlog item with clear acceptance: mitigation applied, p95 back to <200ms for 24h, RCA with root cause and action plan. Also list rollout criteria for future runtime releases (canary size, rollback automation).

marco_garcia (eng-runtime): Created internal ticket INF-7892: "AtlasHealth dedicated throughput regression — emergency mitigation + RCA". Assigning to me for mitigation and to Jia for verification.

jia_wu (eng-oncall): Mitigation applied to ded-az2-78 at 2026-03-19T00:10Z (rolled back to rtx-3.13.8, kv_eviction off). Early metrics: p95 trending down from 980ms -> ~180ms over 15m. Still observing elevated batch wait at times, investigating client-side batching patterns too.

leah_ng (product): Good. Next steps for backlog: scope options for permanent fix (A) revert heuristic globally until we add more telemetry, (B) make eviction opt-in per pool + increase canary windows, (C) tune kernel fallback priorities. Please attach perf diffs and estimated engineering effort to INF-7892. We'll negotiate timeline with sales & customer success.

anika_patel (support): AtlasHealth asked if we can add a permanent setting to their Dedicated contract to pin runtime versions. They're open to dedicated-managed patches but want SLA guarantees.

marco_garcia (eng-runtime): Action items added to INF-7892: collect perf traces across sessions, add finer KV-cache telemetry, add per-pool runtime override APIs, and draft rollback playbook. Rough estimates: 3d telemetry + traces, 2d per-pool override polish, 2w for full rollback automation + canary infra.

leah_ng (product): I'll prioritize this in next sprint planning as a customer-driven roadmap item with a launch criteria doc: acceptance = stable p95 for 72h on ded pools + rollback automation + per-pool override UI + runbook. If engineering needs more scope negotiation, we can stage deliverables.

sam_sullivan (sales): Sharing this with AtlasHealth; thanks for the quick turn. Keep me posted on ETA for permanent fix; they want to know if this is a config or code change.

ops-bot: INF-7892 status update: mitigation applied, p95 improved, RCA in progress.

marco_garcia (eng-runtime): Will post perf diffs and attach kernel logs to INF-7892 by EOD. If anyone sees regression signals from other dedicated pools, please ping this thread.

jia_wu (eng-oncall): Closing the immediate customer-facing loop. Reopen thread if p95 climbs above 400ms again for ded-az2-78.

anika_patel (support): I'll keep AtlasHealth updated and escalate if they hit any new issues. Thanks everyone.
